title: A platform can reactivate a worker after one complaint and later deactivate again before an adjudicated access remedy
source_unit: Fair Work Commission Uber Eats platform reactivation and repeat-deactivation case [2026] FWC 48
geography: Australia; Uber Eats delivery platform, FWC UDE2025/185

observations.period: August 2024 through January 12, 2026; repeated complaint, block, reactivation, deactivation, and order sequence

first_access_episode.value: a 2024 user complaint led to a temporary block, warning, and later reactivation

second_access_episode.value: a second 2025 complaint led to another block, warning, preliminary notice, and final deactivation on July 29, 2025

procedural_finding.value: Commission found warnings and deactivation inconsistent with the Digital Labour Platform Deactivation Code and found no valid reason for final deactivation

remedy.value: reactivation, deemed work from July 20, 2025 until reactivation, and lost-pay quantum to be discussed by the parties

payment_and_durability.unit: missing final reactivation, lost-pay amount, payment receipt, post-order account activity, earnings, recurrence, alternative work, trust, and exit

mechanism.value: Repeated complaint-triggered access interruptions can make platform transparency and recurrence part of the worker's practical control surface; one reactivation does not establish durable access

observations.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission decision [2026] FWC 48 and reactivation order; repeated access events, procedural disclosure, adjudication, and open lost-pay stages are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The public decision does not retain worker identity beyond the case, earnings, trips, household effects, exact lost-pay amount, payment receipt, account durability after reactivation, or later platform/non-platform work.
observations.subgroup: One Uber Eats delivery worker in a public protected-person case; no platform-worker prevalence denominator is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A platform may have legitimate complaint and safety processes, and an adjudicated procedural failure does not establish substantive innocence or later livelihood; formal reactivation is not payment or durable access.

boundary: This record establishes repeated platform-access interruption, procedural adjudication, and a reactivation/lost-pay order. It does not establish final payment, durable access, recovered earnings, alternative work, trust, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the primary FWC decision and order; worker account, trip, complaint, earnings, household, and platform-internal files are not retained.
